title: Multicast: one sender, a group of listeners
summary: Unicast talks to one machine, broadcast to every machine nearby, multicast to those who joined a group. Why a printer shows up in one room and not the next.

text: Most traffic is unicast: one sender, one receiver.
- Broadcast reaches every machine of the local network (IPv4 only; ARP uses it).
- Multicast sends once to a group address; only the machines that joined the group listen. IPv6 has no broadcast: it uses multicast instead.
You use multicast without knowing it.
- mDNS lets machines find each other by name (printer.local) with no DNS server: each one answers questions about its own name.
- VRRP lets a spare router take over the gateway's address when the main one dies.
- An operator sends a TV channel once; its routers copy it only towards homes watching it.
Addresses in 224.0.0.0/24 are link-local: routers never forward them.
- So mDNS works inside one network only. A printer found by name in one office is invisible from another subnet.
- It's not broken: add the printer by its IP address, or ask the network team for an mDNS relay (a reflector).
